fullPassage: Young Change-Makers Shaping the Future There are a lot of things that fill us with hope for the future: technology, science, accountable leaders, and nonprofit organizations committed to doing good. However, few things give us more hope for the future than young people. Some young people are already working toward solutions for the problems their communities and the world are facing. Let’s look at three inspirational examples of these young people. Combating Online Hate with ReThink Trisha Prabhu, a young computer scientist from the U.S., is fighting cyberbullying with her innovative application ReThink. ReThink is a virtual keyboard that uses artificial intelligence to detect potentially hurtful text messages before they are sent and prompts young people to pause and reconsider their words. When a user types a message that contains potentially offensive language, such as “I hate you,” ReThink prompts: “Hold on! Are you sure you want to say that?” or, “Remember. You are what you type!” In 2014, when Trisha was just thirteen years old, she read the tragic news of a twelve-year-old girl who had been cyberbullied for over a year and a half. Shocked at the story, she decided to prevent cyberbullying by using technology and created ReThink. ReThink has been used by schools and organizations worldwide and has successfully raised awareness on cyberbullying. It has helped young people make better decisions in digital space where people could easily be unkind toward each other. In fact, it has been found that when using ReThink, adolescents change their minds 93% of the time and decide not to post offensive messages. Inventing with Discarded Electronic Parts Kelvin Doe, a self-taught inventor and engineer from Sierra Leone, has been fascinated with electronics since childhood. He would often do experiments with discarded electronics he found in trash cans to create his own inventions. In 2009, at the young age of thirteen, Kelvin built his own FM radio station by using a transmitter he made from discarded electronic parts. In 2014, during the time when an Ebola outbreak affected Africa, Kelvin’s radio station proved to be invaluable. With schools closed, his radio station provided educational programs to students over the radio. This was especially important in his country, where the radio was the main source of media. Kelvin also improved the lives of people around him by providing affordable resources. He invented a battery capable of powering homes and small businesses, designed a generator that runs on salt water, and constructed a windmill to supply electricity to his community. Helping Homeless People Rebuild Their Lives John Michael Stagliano is a young social activist from the U.S. who founded Home Again in 2016. It is a nonprofit organization that offers furniture and household essentials to families and individuals transitioning from homelessness to stable housing. He says, “For people who have lived in their cars, in and out of shelters, and in the woods, to be home again is a triumph, a sense of peace, and something to be celebrated.” John’s journey began in 2015. At the age of twelve, he volunteered at a local shelter where people in need were staying. He learned that many of the shelter residents worked hard to rent houses and trailers but faced difficulties in furnishing their new homes upon moving in. This prompted John to decide to do something for those transitioning out of homelessness. Needing donations to gather essential items to help them, John reached out to his family, friends, and neighbors. As word of his efforts spread, donations began to rush in. So John was able to help more people get settled. He said, “I never knew the impact that a simple couch or a kitchen table could have. Furniture can restore the dignity of a family.” Trisha Prabhu, Kelvin Doe, and John Michael Stagliano are all examples of young social activists who have made significant contributions to society. Their innovative efforts to solve social problems demonstrate the power of technology, commitment, and individual initiative. Their stories serve as an inspiration for young people around the world to pursue their passions and make a difference in their communities. As young innovators and social activists keep appearing, they will undoubtedly make the world a better place.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① successful → successfully: 동사 raised를 꾸미므로 형용사가 아니라 부사(successfully)를 써야 한다
det.analysis:
① successful → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'ReThink ~ has successfully raised awareness'는 'ReThink가 성공적으로 인식을 높여 왔다'라는 뜻이 되어야 해요. 여기서 밑줄 자리는 뒤의 동사 raised(높였다)를 꾸며 주는 자리예요. 동사를 꾸밀 때는 형용사가 아니라 부사를 써야 하므로 successful(형용사)이 아니라 successfully(부사)로 고쳐야 맞아요. ❌ successful은 틀림 ←정답

② make: 'It has helped young people make better decisions'는 'ReThink가 청소년이 더 나은 결정을 내리도록 도왔다'예요. 'help + 목적어 + 동사원형(help A do)' 구조라서 make(동사원형)가 맞아요. help 뒤에는 to make도 되고 make도 되니 원형 make는 올바른 형태예요. ✅ 올바름

③ self-taught: 'a self-taught inventor and engineer'는 '독학한 발명가이자 기술자'예요. inventor를 앞에서 꾸미는 형용사 자리라 self-taught(독학한)가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ fascinated: 'Kelvin Doe ~ has been fascinated with electronics'는 '켈빈은 전자기기에 매료되어 왔다'예요. 사람이 무엇에 '매료되는' 것은 감정을 받는 쪽이라 수동형 be fascinated with가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 동사를 꾸미면 부사: raised(동사)를 꾸미니 successfully(부사)

questions.passage: Helping Homeless People Rebuild Their Lives John Michael Stagliano is a young social activist from the U. S.  ①<u>who founded</u> Home Again in 2016.  It is a nonprofit organization that offers furniture and household essentials to families and individuals ②<u>transitioning</u> from homelessness to stable housing.  He says, “For people who ③<u>have lived</u> in their cars, in and out of shelters, and in the woods, to be home again is a triumph, a sense of peace, and something ④<u>to celebrate</u>. ” John’s journey began in 2015.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ to celebrate → to be celebrated: something이 '축하받는' 대상(수동)이므로 to부정사의 수동태 to be celebrated를 쓴다
det.analysis:
① who founded: 'John Michael Stagliano ~ who founded Home Again in 2016'은 '2016년에 Home Again을 설립한 John'이에요. 사람 John을 가리키며 뒤 동사(founded)의 주어 역할을 하니 주격 관계대명사 who가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② transitioning: 'families and individuals transitioning from homelessness to stable housing'은 '노숙에서 안정된 주거로 옮겨 가는 가족과 개인들'이에요. 사람들이 스스로 '옮겨 가는' 능동 관계라 앞 명사를 꾸미는 현재분사 transitioning이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ have lived: 'For people who have lived in their cars'는 '차 안에서 살아온 사람들'이에요. 과거부터 지금까지 이어진 경험이라 현재완료 have lived가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ to celebrate → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'something to be celebrated'는 '축하받아야 할 어떤 것'이라는 뜻이 되어야 해요. 여기서 something은 '축하하는' 게 아니라 '축하받는' 대상이에요. 그래서 to부정사도 수동의 뜻을 담아 to be celebrated(수동태)로 써야 해요. 능동형 to celebrate는 'something이 무언가를 축하한다'가 되어 뜻이 어긋나므로 틀려요. ❌ to celebrate는 틀림 ←정답
det.tip: 명사가 '~받는' 대상이면 to부정사도 수동태: something to be celebrated(축하받을 것)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② demonstrates → demonstrate: 진짜 주어가 복수인 efforts이므로 복수 동사 demonstrate를 쓴다
det.analysis:
① who have made: 'young social activists who have made significant contributions'는 '중요한 기여를 해 온 젊은 사회 운동가들'이에요. 선행사가 activists(복수)라 have made가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② demonstrates → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'Their innovative efforts to solve social problems demonstrate the power of technology'는 '사회 문제를 해결하려는 그들의 혁신적 노력은 기술의 힘을 보여 준다'예요. 문장의 진짜 주어는 'Their innovative efforts(그들의 혁신적 노력들)'로 복수예요. 중간에 낀 'to solve social problems(사회 문제를 해결하려는)'의 problems에 속으면 안 돼요. 복수 주어 efforts에는 복수 동사 demonstrate를 써야 하므로 단수형 demonstrates는 틀려요. ❌ demonstrates는 틀림 ←정답

③ to pursue: 'an inspiration ~ to pursue their passions'는 '자신의 열정을 좇도록 하는 영감'이에요. 앞의 명사를 꾸미며 '~하도록'의 뜻을 담은 to부정사라 to pursue가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ will undoubtedly make: 'they will undoubtedly make the world a better place'는 '그들은 틀림없이 세상을 더 나은 곳으로 만들 것이다'예요. 조동사 will 뒤에는 동사원형이 오니 make가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 긴 주어에 속지 말 것: 진짜 주어 efforts(복수) → demonstrate(복수 동사)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ rush → pause: ReThink는 사용자가 '멈춰서(pause)' 다시 생각하게 하는 앱이므로 pause가 맞다
det.analysis:
① innovative: 'her innovative application ReThink'는 '그녀의 혁신적인 앱 ReThink'예요. 새로운 방식의 앱이라 '혁신적인(innovative)'이 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절

② virtual: 'ReThink is a virtual keyboard'는 'ReThink는 가상 키보드이다'예요. 스마트폰 화면 속 키보드라 '가상의(virtual)'가 맞아요. ✅ 적절

③ rush → 여기가 정답(부적절한 곳)! 원문은 'prompts young people to pause and reconsider their words'로 'ReThink는 청소년이 멈춰서 자신의 말을 다시 생각하도록 유도한다'예요. ReThink의 핵심은 메시지를 보내기 전에 '잠깐 멈추게(pause)' 하는 것이에요. '서두르다(rush)'는 정반대라 문맥에 안 맞아요. ❌ 부적절 ←정답

④ worldwide: 'ReThink has been used by schools and organizations worldwide'는 'ReThink는 전 세계 학교와 단체에서 사용되어 왔다'예요. 뒤에 전 세계적 성공이 이어지니 '전 세계에서(worldwide)'가 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절
det.tip: ReThink = 멈춰서 다시 생각하게 함 → pause(멈추다), rush(서두르다)는 반대

questions.passage: In 2014, during the time when an Ebola outbreak affected Africa, Kelvin’s radio station proved to be invaluable.  With schools closed, his radio station provided ①<u>recreational</u> programs to students over the radio. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① recreational → educational: 학교가 문을 닫아 라디오가 '교육(educational)' 프로그램을 대신 제공한 것이므로 educational이 맞다
det.analysis:
① recreational → 여기가 정답(부적절한 곳)! 원문은 'With schools closed, his radio station provided educational programs to students over the radio'로 '학교가 문을 닫자 그의 라디오 방송국이 학생들에게 교육 프로그램을 제공했다'예요. 학교가 못 열려서 라디오가 수업을 대신했다는 흐름이라 '교육적인(educational)' 프로그램이어야 해요. '오락용(recreational)'은 학교 수업을 대신한다는 문맥과 어긋나요. ❌ 부적절 ←정답

② main: 'the radio was the main source of media'는 '라디오가 주된 매체였다'예요. 뒤에서 라디오 방송이 특히 중요했다고 했으니 '주된(main)'이 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절

③ powering: 'a battery capable of powering homes and small businesses'는 '가정과 소규모 사업체에 전력을 공급할 수 있는 배터리'예요. 배터리의 기능이라 '전력을 공급하는(powering)'이 맞아요. ✅ 적절

④ supply: 'constructed a windmill to supply electricity to his community'는 '지역사회에 전기를 공급하기 위해 풍차를 만들었다'예요. 풍차로 전기를 '공급한다(supply)'가 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절
det.tip: 학교 대신 라디오가 수업 제공 → educational(교육적인), recreational(오락용)은 어긋남

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ④ powering homes and small businesses(가정과 소규모 사업체에 전력을 공급하는 것): 배터리·발전기·풍차로 전기를 공급했다는 흐름
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'He invented a battery capable of ___, designed a generator that runs on salt water, and constructed a windmill to supply electricity to his community.'(그는 ___할 수 있는 배터리를 발명하고, 소금물로 작동하는 발전기를 설계하고, 지역사회에 전기를 공급할 풍차를 만들었다.) 배터리·발전기·풍차가 나란히 나오고 마지막에 '전기를 공급한다(supply electricity)'가 있으니, 배터리도 전력과 관련된 기능이어야 해요.

❌ ① cleaning polluted ocean water(오염된 바닷물을 정화하는 것): 물 정화 이야기는 나오지 않아요.

❌ ② broadcasting live radio signals(라디오 신호를 생중계하는 것): 라디오는 앞 문단의 다른 장치예요. 배터리의 기능이 아니에요.

❌ ③ storing emergency medical supplies(비상 의료 물자를 보관하는 것): 의료 물자 보관은 언급되지 않아요.

✅ ④ powering homes and small businesses(가정과 소규모 사업체에 전력을 공급하는 것): 뒤의 발전기·풍차와 함께 '전력 공급'이라는 흐름에 딱 맞아요. ←정답
det.tip: 배터리 → 발전기 → 풍차(전기 공급) 나열 → 배터리도 '전력 공급' 기능

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ② gather essential items(필수 물품을 모으는 것): 이사한 사람들의 집을 채울 물품을 모으려고 기부가 필요했다는 흐름
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'Needing donations to ___ to help them, John reached out to his family, friends, and neighbors.'(그들을 돕기 위해 ___할 기부가 필요해서, John은 가족·친구·이웃에게 도움을 청했다.) 앞에서 쉼터 거주자들이 새 집에 '살림살이를 채우는 데(furnishing their new homes)' 어려움을 겪었다고 했고, John은 그들에게 가구와 생활필수품을 지원해요. 그러니 기부는 '필수 물품을 모으기' 위한 것이어야 해요.

❌ ① build affordable new houses(저렴한 새 집을 짓는 것): John은 집을 직접 짓는 게 아니라 이미 얻은 집을 채우도록 도와요.

✅ ② gather essential items(필수 물품을 모으는 것): 새 집에 필요한 살림살이를 모은다는 흐름과 딱 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ③ train more volunteer workers(더 많은 자원봉사자를 훈련하는 것): 자원봉사자 훈련 이야기는 나오지 않아요.

❌ ④ host large public events(대규모 공개 행사를 여는 것): 행사 개최는 언급되지 않아요.
det.tip: 새 집을 채울 살림살이가 필요 → 기부로 '필수 물품을 모으다(gather essential items)'

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ③ 원문 근거: Trisha Prabhu, a young computer scientist from the U.S., is fighting cyberbullying
det.analysis:
❌ ① 원문은 'In 2014, when Trisha was just thirteen years old'로, Trisha가 소식을 접한 때는 '열세 살'이에요. '열다섯 살'은 나이가 달라 틀려요.

questions.passage: Helping Homeless People Rebuild Their Lives John Michael Stagliano is a young social activist from the U. S.  who founded Home Again in 2016.  It is a nonprofit organization that offers furniture and household essentials to families and individuals transitioning from homelessness to stable housing.  He says, “For people who have lived in their cars, in and out of shelters, and in the woods, to be home again is a triumph, a sense of peace, and something to be celebrated. ” John’s journey began in 2015. So John was able to help more people get settled.  He said, “I never knew the impact that a simple couch or a kitchen table could have.

questions.passage: Young Change-Makers Shaping the Future There are a lot of things that fill us with hope for the future: technology, science, accountable leaders, and nonprofit organizations committed to doing good.  However, few things give us more hope for the future than young people.  Some young people are already working toward solutions for the problems their communities and the world are facing.  Let’s look at three inspirational examples of these young people.  Combating Online Hate with ReThink Trisha Prabhu, a young computer scientist from the U. S. , is fighting cyberbullying with her innovative application ReThink.  ReThink is a virtual keyboard that uses artificial intelligence to detect potentially hurtful text messages before they are sent and prompts young people to pause and reconsider their words.  When a user types a message that contains potentially offensive language, such as “I hate you,” ReThink prompts: “Hold on!  Are you sure you want to say that? ” or, “Remember.  You are what you type! ” In 2014, when Trisha was just thirteen years old, she read the tragic news of a twelve-year-old girl who had been cyberbullied for over a year and a half.  Shocked at the story, she decided to prevent cyberbullying by using technology and created ReThink.  ReThink has been used by schools and organizations worldwide and has successfully raised awareness on cyberbullying.  It has helped young people make better decisions in digital space where people could easily be unkind toward each other.  In fact, it has been found that when using ReThink, adolescents change their minds 93% of the time and decide not to post offensive messages.  Inventing with Discarded Electronic Parts Kelvin Doe, a self-taught inventor and engineer from Sierra Leone, has been fascinated with electronics since childhood.  He would often do experiments with discarded electronics he found in trash cans to create his own inventions.  In 2009, at the young age of thirteen, Kelvin built his own FM radio station by using a transmitter he made from discarded electronic parts.  In 2014, during the time when an Ebola outbreak affected Africa, Kelvin’s radio station proved to be invaluable.  With schools closed, his radio station provided educational programs to students over the radio.  This was especially important in his country, where the radio was the main source of media.  Kelvin also improved the lives of people around him by providing affordable resources.  He invented a battery capable of powering homes and small businesses, designed a generator that runs on salt water, and constructed a windmill to supply electricity to his community.  Helping Homeless People Rebuild Their Lives John Michael Stagliano is a young social activist from the U. S.  who founded Home Again in 2016.  It is a nonprofit organization that offers furniture and household essentials to families and individuals transitioning from homelessness to stable housing.  He says, “For people who have lived in their cars, in and out of shelters, and in the woods, to be home again is a triumph, a sense of peace, and something to be celebrated. ” John’s journey began in 2015.  At the age of twelve, he volunteered at a local shelter where people in need were staying.  He learned that many of the shelter residents worked hard to rent houses and trailers but faced difficulties in furnishing their new homes upon moving in.  This prompted John to decide to do something for those transitioning out of homelessness.  Needing donations to gather essential items to help them, John reached out to his family, friends, and neighbors.  As word of his efforts spread, donations began to rush in.  So John was able to help more people get settled.  He said, “I never knew the impact that a simple couch or a kitchen table could have.  Furniture can restore the dignity of a family. ” Trisha Prabhu, Kelvin Doe, and John Michael Stagliano are all examples of young social activists who have made significant contributions to society.  Their innovative efforts to solve social problems demonstrate the power of technology, commitment, and individual initiative.  Their stories serve as an inspiration for young people around the world to pursue their passions and make a difference in their communities.

❌ ② 기부를 보낸 자원봉사자들은 돕는 쪽이지 도움을 받는 대상이 아니에요.

❌ ③ Home Again을 함께 세운 동료들은 본문에 나오지 않아요.

✅ ④ 지역 쉼터에 머무르던, 도움이 필요한 사람들: John이 도우려 한 대상과 정확히 일치해요. ←정답
det.tip: them = John이 '돕고자(to help)' 한 대상 = 쉼터의 도움이 필요한 사람들

ch: Home Again을 John과 함께 세운 동료들
지역 쉼터에 머무르던, 도움이 필요한 사람들

questions.passage: Young Change-Makers Shaping the Future There are a lot of things that fill us with hope for the future: technology, science, accountable leaders, and nonprofit organizations committed to __________.  However, few things give us more hope for the future than young people.  Some young people are already working toward solutions for the problems their communities and the world are facing.  Let’s look at three inspirational examples of these young people.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ② doing good(선한 일을 하는 것): 미래에 희망을 주는 좋은 것들을 나열하는 긍정적 흐름
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'There are a lot of things that fill us with hope for the future: technology, science, accountable leaders, and nonprofit organizations committed to ___.'(미래에 희망을 주는 것이 많다: 기술, 과학, 책임감 있는 지도자들, 그리고 ___에 헌신하는 비영리 단체들.) 희망을 주는 좋은 것들을 나열하는 흐름이고, 비영리 단체(nonprofit)는 이익이 아니라 좋은 목적을 위해 일하는 곳이에요.

❌ ① making large profits(큰 이익을 내는 것): 비영리(nonprofit) 단체는 이익 추구가 목적이 아니라서 어긋나요.

✅ ② doing good(선한 일을 하는 것): 비영리 단체가 헌신하는 대상이자 '희망을 주는 좋은 것'이라는 흐름과 딱 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ③ winning global awards(세계적인 상을 받는 것): 상을 받으려 헌신한다는 내용은 없어요.

❌ ④ gaining political power(정치 권력을 얻는 것): 권력 추구는 희망을 주는 긍정적 흐름과 반대예요.
det.tip: nonprofit(비영리) 단체가 헌신하는 것 = 이익이 아니라 '선한 일(doing good)'

questions.passage: Inventing with Discarded Electronic Parts Kelvin Doe, a self-taught inventor and engineer from Sierra Leone, has been fascinated with electronics since childhood.  He would often do experiments with discarded electronics he found in trash cans to create his own inventions.  In 2009, at the young age of thirteen, __________ by using a transmitter he made from discarded electronic parts.  In 2014, during the time when an Ebola outbreak affected Africa, Kelvin’s radio station proved to be invaluable.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"Kelvin은 자신만의 FM 라디오 방송국을 세웠다." (7단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) built, FM, his, Kelvin, own, radio, station 을 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 7단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: Kelvin built his own FM radio station
det.analysis:
주어는 사람 이름 'Kelvin'이고, '세웠다'는 과거의 일이라 과거형 동사 built로 나타내요: Kelvin built(켈빈이 세웠다).

무엇을 세웠는지 그 목적어는 '자신만의 FM 라디오 방송국'이에요. '자신만의'는 소유격 his에 강조하는 own을 더해 his own(자신만의)으로 쓰고, 그 뒤에 FM radio station(FM 라디오 방송국)을 이어요.

순서대로 이으면 Kelvin / built / his / own / FM / radio / station.
det.tip: his own = 자신만의 (소유격 + own) / built = build의 과거형

questions.wa: Kelvin built his own FM radio station
accept: Kelvin built his own FM radio station

questions.passage: In 2014, during the time when an Ebola outbreak affected Africa, Kelvin’s radio station proved to be invaluable.  With schools closed, his radio station provided educational programs to students over the radio.  This was especially important in his country, where the radio was the main source of media.  Kelvin also improved the lives of people around him by providing affordable resources.  He invented a battery capable of powering homes and small businesses, ①<u>designing</u> a generator that runs on salt water, and constructed a windmill to supply electricity to his community.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①은 어법상 틀렸다. 어법에 맞게 올바른 형태로 고쳐 쓰시오. (한 단어, 영어로)

det.korean: designing → designed: invented, constructed와 대등하게 연결된 병렬이므로 과거형 designed
det.analysis:
밑줄이 있는 문장은 'He invented a battery ~, ①<u>designing</u> a generator that runs on salt water, and constructed a windmill ~'이에요. '그는 배터리를 발명하고, 발전기를 설계하고, 풍차를 만들었다'라는 뜻이에요.

여기서 세 가지 행동 'invented(발명했다) ~ designed(설계했다) ~ and constructed(만들었다)'는 and로 대등하게 이어지는 병렬 구조예요. 병렬로 연결되는 말들은 형태를 똑같이 맞춰야 해요. 앞뒤가 과거형 동사(invented, constructed)이므로, 가운데도 과거형 동사 designed로 써야 맞아요.

밑줄처럼 designing(현재분사)으로 쓰면 앞뒤의 과거형 동사와 형태가 어긋나 병렬이 깨져요. 그래서 designed로 고쳐야 맞아요.
det.tip: A, B, and C 병렬 = 형태 일치: invented / designed / constructed (모두 과거형)

questions.passage: Young Change-Makers Shaping the Future There are a lot of things that fill us with hope for the future: technology, science, accountable leaders, and nonprofit organizations committed to doing good.  However, __________.  Some young people are already working toward solutions for the problems their communities and the world are facing.  Let’s look at three inspirational examples of these young people.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"젊은이들보다 우리에게 미래에 대한 더 많은 희망을 주는 것은 거의 없다." (12단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) few, for, future, give, hope, more, people, than, the, things, us, young 을 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 12단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: few things give us more hope for the future than young people
det.analysis:
'~한 것은 거의 없다'는 '거의 없는'을 뜻하는 few를 주어에 써서 나타내요: few things(거의 없는 것들 → ~한 것은 거의 없다). '~을 (누구에게) 준다'는 'give + 사람 + 사물' 어순이라 give us more hope(우리에게 더 많은 희망을 준다)로 이어요.

무엇에 대한 희망인지는 for the future(미래에 대한)로 나타내요. '젊은이들보다'라는 비교는 비교급 more와 짝을 이루는 than을 써서 than young people(젊은이들보다)로 마무리해요.

순서대로 이으면 few / things / give / us / more / hope / for / the / future / than / young / people. (더 많은 희망을 주는 것이 젊은이들보다 적다 → 젊은이가 가장 큰 희망이라는 뜻)
det.tip: few things = ~한 것은 거의 없다 / more ~ than = ~보다 더 많은

questions.wa: few things give us more hope for the future than young people
accept: few things give us more hope for the future than young people

questions.passage: ” John’s journey began in 2015.  At the age of twelve, he volunteered at a local shelter where people in need were staying.  He learned that many of the shelter residents worked hard to rent houses and trailers but faced difficulties in furnishing their new homes upon moving in.  __________ for those transitioning out of homelessness.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오.
"이것이 John이 무언가를 하기로 결심하게 만들었다."

[ decide / do / John / prompted / something / This / to / to ] (8단어) (영어로)

det.korean: This prompted John to decide to do something
det.analysis:
주어 'This(이것이)'로 시작하고, '~하게 만들었다'를 뜻하는 과거형 동사 prompted를 이어요. 'prompt + 사람 + to + 동사원형(~가 …하도록 만들다)' 구조라, 사람 John 뒤에 to decide(결심하도록)를 놓아요: This prompted John to decide.

무엇을 결심했는지는 다시 'to + 동사원형'으로 '무언가를 하기로'를 나타내요: to do something(무언가를 하기로). decide 뒤에도 to부정사가 오므로 to do가 이어져요.

순서대로 이으면 This / prompted / John / to / decide / to / do / something.
det.tip: prompt A to do = A가 ~하도록 만들다 / decide to do = ~하기로 결심하다

questions.wa: This prompted John to decide to do something
accept: This prompted John to decide to do something

questions.passage: It is a nonprofit organization that offers furniture and household essentials to families and individuals transitioning from homelessness to stable housing.  He says, “For people who have lived in their cars, in and out of shelters, and in the woods, to be home again is a triumph, a sense of peace, and something to be celebrated. ” John’s journey began in 2015.  At the age of twelve, __________.  He learned that many of the shelter residents worked hard to rent houses and trailers but faced difficulties in furnishing their new homes upon moving in.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"그는 도움이 필요한 사람들이 머무르던 지역 쉼터에서 자원봉사를 했다." (12단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) a, at, he, in, local, need, people, shelter, staying, volunteered, were, where 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 12단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: he volunteered at a local shelter where people in need were staying
det.analysis:
주어 'he(그는)'로 시작하고 '자원봉사를 했다'는 과거형 volunteered로 나타내요. 어디에서 했는지는 장소를 나타내는 전치사 at을 써서 at a local shelter(지역 쉼터에서)로 이어요.

그 쉼터가 어떤 곳인지 꾸며 주려고 장소를 받는 관계부사 where를 쓰고, 그 안에 '도움이 필요한 사람들이 머무르던'을 넣어요. '도움이 필요한 사람들'은 people in need, '머무르던'은 과거진행형 were staying으로 나타내요: where people in need were staying.

순서대로 이으면 he / volunteered / at / a / local / shelter / where / people / in / need / were / staying.
det.tip: 관계부사 where = 장소를 꾸밈 / people in need = 도움이 필요한 사람들 / were staying = 머무르고 있었다

questions.wa: he volunteered at a local shelter where people in need were staying
accept: he volunteered at a local shelter where people in need were staying
